children: Artificial-intelligence jitters and fresh tariff risks are testing the U.S. dollar, but it's still too early to bet against it, OCBC FX strategist Sim Moh Siong says in a note. Sticky inflation, resilient U.S. growth and the risk of a more hawkish Fed should keep the currency supported through 1H of 2027, the analyst says. A gradual decline is more likely in 2H of 2027, as lower energy prices reduce the risk of further Fed tightening. Easing political uncertainty in Europe could also improve the appeal of European assets, Sim says. The ICE U.S. Dollar Index is up 0.1% at 103.88, according to LSEG data. (venkat.pr@wsj.com)
